Nephrotic syndrome is a group of symptoms caused by kidney damage that leads to swelling and leakage of body fluids from blood into tissues. It can occur in people with diabetes and/or heart disease, or after surgery or trauma. Some forms of nephrotic syndrome, such as minimal change disease, are related to an autoimmune response of the body's immune system. 

Patients who have nephrotic syndrome may experience swelling (edema) in their legs; weight gain due to water build-up; frequent urination day and night; increased thirst due to increased water intake; loss of appetite; tiredness; nausea; vomiting; and a thickened skin (more than normal). Other symptoms include high levels of cholesterol in blood, protein in urine, and waste products such as urea or creatinine (waste materials that are normally filtered out via the kidneys).

Treatment for nephrotic syndrome depends on the cause of the kidney damage, which may vary depending on the type of nephrotic syndrome. In general, nephrotic patients need to keep their blood cholesterol and blood pressure under control to prevent further kidney health damage. Someone at risk for nephrotic syndrome should eat less salty foods and consume a diet to reduce inflammation in the kidneys (anti-inflammatory food) like fruits

Solution:
We use the power rule for differentiation which states that the derivative of x^n is n*x^(n-1) for any real number n. We can break down the function into three simpler parts:

f(x) = x^2 + 3x - 5

Taking the derivative of each term separately:
d/dx [x^2] = 2x 
d/dx [3x] = 3
d/dx [-5] = 0

Now we take the sum of the derivatives for each part:
d/dx [f(x)] = d/dx [x^2] + d/dx [3x] + d/dx [-5]
d/dx [f(x)] = 2x + 3

    library(httr)
    library(jsonlite)

    #Set your Open AI API key 
    system("export OPENAI_API_KEY='your-api-key'")
    
    #Create function to revice api response in json schema
    get_ai_response <- function(prompt) {
       # Create the request message
       req_url <- paste0("https://api.openai.com/v1/engines/davinci/completions", "?prompt=", prompt) 
       
       # Execute the GET request with the API key as authorization header
       req_data <- httr::GET(
         url = req_url,
         add_headers(.headers = c(API_KEY = system("echo $OPENAI_API_KEY")))
       )
       
       # Convert the response body into JSON
       res_body <- content(req_data, "parsed")
        
       # Return the prompt
       return(res_body[["text"]])      
    }
